Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

The Director, Information Management will lead the Information Management practice across the Infrastructure Segment in Canada, overseeing the core capability streams of BIM, GIS/Digital Twin, and Document Control. This role is responsible for ensuring strategic alignment, integration, and governance across supporting digital services including Program Management Information Systems (PMIS) and Data Engineering.

The successful candidate will also serve as the Information Management Lead on a major aviation program, overseeing Document Control, BIM, and PMIS functions while providing executive-level client engagement and strategic leadership. jobs.title: Director of Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Blackpoint Cyber is the leading provider of world-class cybersecurity threat hunting, detection and remediation technology. Founded by former National Security Agency (NSA) cyber operations experts who applied their learnings to bring national security-grade technology solutions to commercial customers around the world, Blackpoint Cyber is in hyper-growth mode, fueled by a recent $190m series C round.

Company Culture

At Blackpoint Cyber, we value high-quality execution, ownership, and strong morals. Our principles are never tested, and we are proud to always do right by our customers. We are an energetic and collaborative team that maintains a high-performance culture and enables growth by overcoming challenges in the modern cyber threat landscape. If you are a driven professional with a passion for learning and contributing at a high level, Blackpoint Cyber welcomes you.

Position Overview

Blackpoint Cyber is seeking a strategic and visionary Director of Platform Engineering to lead the development and execution of its Unified Security Posture data platform, which powers the company’s data-centric cybersecurity solutions. This leader will serve as the single-threaded owner for the roadmap and operations of the cloud-based platform, including vendor integrations, developer and data tooling, identity, authentication, tenant management, and other core services.

This role will drive vision and execution across multiple engineering teams, working cross-functionally with internal stakeholders, product leaders, and site reliability engineering partners. The Director of Platform Engineering will translate business and technical needs into clear strategies, oversee roadmap execution and service quality, and build a high-performing organization through strong hiring, mentorship, and technical leadership. As a highly visible leader, this person will also help establish company-wide operational excellence practices for instrumentation, incident response, root cause analysis, and remediation.

Key Responsibilities

Define and drive the platform roadmap aligned with product and business goals.
Partner across the Product organization and SRE team to ensure platform security, reliability, and scalability.
Lead the development of the data pipeline, integrating with Blackpoint’s endpoint agent and vendor data, including storage, tiered access, and query capabilities.
Deliver platform services and public APIs supporting core functions such as tenant management, identity, and role-based access control.
Lead platform tooling and APIs that accelerate AI/ML and business intelligence initiatives.
Oversee developer productivity tooling, including CI/CD systems.
Define the long-term vision for the data platform by implementing best practices in data architecture, modeling, and governance, while staying current on emerging technologies and trends.
Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and partners.
Foster excellence in platform reliability, scalability, security, and software quality.
Hire, develop, and grow a high-caliber team of platform and data engineers, scaling the team and organizational structure as needed.
Drive the adoption of AI across the development lifecycle (AI DLC) to increase engineering productivity, accelerate delivery, improve software quality, and enable teams to build and deliver high-quality products more efficiently

Qualifications

15+ years of experience in software development, preferably in cybersecurity, including at least 5 years of people management experience leading multiple teams.
Proven experience leading a Platform Engineering function at the Director level.
5+ years of experience working with large-scale AWS cloud solutions and technologies such as Postgres, Elastic, Redis, streaming data platforms, and ETL processes.
Hands-on experience architecting and building complex data platforms and service integrations.
Deep knowledge of CI/CD, production deployment at scale, and data pipeline orchestration.
Demonstrated ability to drive high-impact initiatives and long-term strategic goals.
Strong leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Why Join Blackpoint Cyber

If you are passionate about cybersecurity and have a proven track record of leading and managing software engineering teams, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity. Blackpoint Cyber offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a dynamic work environment where you can make a real impact in the field of cybersecurity.

Blackpoint Cyber welcomes and encourages applications from qualified individuals of all races, colors, religions, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, or any other legally protected status. We are committed to equality of opportunity in all aspects of employment.

For eligible employees in the US, Blackpoint offers competitive Health, Vision, Dental, and Life Insurance plans, a robust 401k plan, Discretionary Time Off, and other minor perks. International employees receive competitive benefits in accordance with local market standards and applicable country requirements.

Blackpoint believes all employees should share in the company’s success – equity participation is available to employees globally, with program details varying by location and employment structure.

About Us

Nova Scotia is rich in natural resources - including biodiversity, forests, geological resources, provincial parks and the land we manage. The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for the development, management, conversation and protection of forest, mineral, parks and wildlife resources and the administration of the province's crown land. Together, we are working with Nova Scotians to build a better future through sustainable natural resource management as we all benefit from the natural health and wealth of the province.

About Our Opportunity

As Director, Strategic Policy and Planning, you provide leadership in facilitating appropriate linkages between policy, program and delivery structures, and developing new inclusive approaches which will generate greater collective knowledge and enhance capacity for integrated, collaborative policy planning, legislative and regulatory development.

In addition, you provide strategic direction and oversight for the research, design, planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of department strategies and initiatives.

Further, you are responsible for directing a team of policy professionals, including maintaining appropriate relationships with central agencies (ECO, OSE, FTB), and directing and ensuring the quality of DNR and DOE submissions to Executive Council.

Primary Accountabilities

Lead and develop an effective, coordinated strategic planning infrastructure with associated policy, planning and regulatory management processes, change management, standards and guidelines for DNR/DOE.
Lead policy/planning initiatives, with an emphasis on those related to key natural resource and energy strategies.
Provide broad oversight for environmental scanning and analyses to monitor trends, identify gaps and risks in internal planning activities and to inform and stimulate discussion about future strategic directions and opportunities that might affect policy and planning decisions.
Provide oversight for the development and coordination of legislative planning and response during the Legislative Sessions of the House.
Oversee and directs the development of departmental Memos to Executive Council, R&Rs, legislative requests, Briefing Books, and all Committee appearances for DNR and DOE.
Provide a planned approach to increase internal capacity and build and sustain required skill sets of the team to meet current and future needs, ensuring the policy and planning team are properly resourced, motivated, empowered and have access to opportunities for growth and development.

jobs.description:
About Inline

Inline is a Canadian mid-sized and growing civil engineering field services company of 550+ people, founded in 2012. We provide geomatics, materials testing, and geotechnical and environmental engineering to land development, infrastructure, oil and gas, industrial and mining clients, from nine branches across Western Canada and the North and operations in the United States. We have completed two acquisitions, most recently Challenger Geomatics in 2026, and are executing a five-year plan built on organic growth and further acquisitions. We have more than 90 employee shareholders and more than 20 Indigenous partners.

Inline has been named one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures and certified as a Great Place to Work.

Role Overview

Position Title: Chief Financial Officer
Department: Finance
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer
Direct Reports: Controller; Vice President, Finance and Integration
Works Closely With: Senior Leadership Team, Operations, People Operations, IT, the Board, lenders, auditors and partners
Location: Edmonton/Acheson, Alberta preferred; open to Calgary

The CFO leads Inline's finance function and is the CEO's partner on strategy, capital and acquisitions. The Controller runs the close and day-to-day reporting; the CFO oversees that work, sets direction, funds the plan and leads the finance side of growth. This is a hands-on role in a founder-led and operator-first company. You’ll work alongside operational leaders to give them reliable financial information, plan ahead for cash and capital needs, and lead the financial integration of new acquisitions.

Key Accountabilities

1.Strategy & Capital
Help the CEO and Senior Leadership Team decide where Inline plays and how it wins.
Partner with the CEO on the five-year plan, capital allocation and the balance between organic growth and acquisitions.
Lead budgeting, forecasting and long-range planning, and report results to the Senior Leadership Team and the Board.
Manage the mix, not just the total: margin by service line, sector and geography, and client concentration.

2.Treasury & Cash
Keep the business funded through seasonal swings and growth.
Manage cash flow and working capital through a highly seasonal business with a strong spring ramp-up.
Own lender relationships, credit facilities and equipment financing for a large fleet.
Manage deferred and vendor-financed acquisition payments.

3.Acquisitions & Integration
Make acquisitions a repeatable strength.
Lead financial due diligence, valuation, deal structure and closing, including working capital adjustments.
With the VP, Finance and Integration, fully integrate acquired companies: systems, processes, reporting and compensation.
Build a repeatable acquisition and integration playbook.

4.Field to Finance
Turn the work done in the field into accurate invoices, margin and cash.
Make sure field records, cost coding and invoices are right the first time, so billing and collections move fast.
Give business unit and project leaders margin data they can act on.
Lead the rollout of our new ERP across the group.

5.Oversight & Employee Ownership
Keep the numbers trusted and our employee-owners informed.
Oversee the close, reporting, audit and controls led by the Controller, across Canadian and U.S. entities.
Oversee accounting for our Indigenous partnerships and joint ventures.
Steward our employee share program: valuations, share transactions, liquidity planning and communication with employee-owners.

6.Finance Team
Build a finance team people want to join and stay on.
Lead and develop the Controller, the VP, Finance and Integration, and the finance team.
Bring finance into the field: help operations leaders understand and own their numbers.

What Success Looks Like in the First 12–18 Months

The ERP (Deltek / Vantage Point) goes live across the group on schedule and within budget, with Finance and Operations using it in their day-to-day work.
Challenger is fully integrated into Inline’s systems, processes, and reporting, and a documented integration playbook is ready for the next acquisition.
At least one new acquisition closes, with Finance leading the integration.
The time it takes to issue invoices and collect payment decreases measurably.
A rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and an annual capital plan help Inline anticipate and manage seasonal cash needs.
All entities complete a clean year-end audit.
The Finance team is stable and engaged, with clearly defined roles and responsibilities.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

CPA required; an MBA is an asset.
15+ years of progressive finance experience, including 5+ as a CFO or VP Finance.
Has bought and integrated several companies, from diligence through integration.
Experience in a project-based business such as engineering, construction or field services, including project accounting.
Experience in a multi-entity, multi-region, asset-heavy company of several hundred people.
Has successfully led an ERP implementation for a project-based business.
Experience with employee share ownership plans, Canada–U.S. cross-border financial operations, or accounting for Indigenous partnerships or joint ventures is an asset.

Skills

Strong commercial judgement: you understand how projects, crews and equipment turn into margin.
Credible with field leaders: you can explain margin to a site manager.
A builder, comfortable creating structure in a fast-growing company.
Hands-on: willing to do the work as well as lead it.

Our Core Values

Humble : Built from the ground up and have not forgotten where we came from.
Adaptable: There is always a way; you just need to find it.
Personable : Polite, courteous and straightforward.
Professional: Integrity, ethical and responsible for our actions.
Productive & Hardworking: We earn what we have.

Location & Compensation

Full-time, based in Edmonton/Acheson, Alberta (preferred) or Calgary, with regular travel to our branches and U.S. operations.
Base salary, a short-term incentive plan, a long-term incentive plan in stock options, and benefits.
The Chief Financial Officer position is fully on-site, with an in-person presence required to lead the Finance team and work closely with executive and operational leaders.

About TandemLaunch

TandemLaunch is a Canadian venture studio. Since 2010 we have created 30+ deep-tech ventures with a combined portfolio value exceeding $700M. We commercialize innovations in consumer electronics, hardware-enabled technologies, machine learning, and embedded systems, working directly with researchers from major university labs. We are one of very few venture studios globally with 15+ years of track record in building successful companies on research-backed deep tech.

About the Role

We are hiring a Director of Product Strategy and Commercialization to be the product-and-market voice inside several of our ventures at once.

These are companies with IP-backed technologies from cutting edge university research, a founding team, and on their first steps to commercial traction. Your job is to support our founders in identifying who would pay, get in front of them, carry the conversation through technical evaluation to a paid pilot or a design win, and feed what you learn back into what the venture builds next.

This is a leadership-track role that hinges on your ability to mentor and influence growing leaders. You will join our venture development team to help our ventures reach the necessary commercial traction to secure their next stage of financing.

What You'll Do

Own customer and partner engagements end-to-end
— from first conversation, through technical evaluation, to a paid pilot or design win. You find the buyer, you get the meeting, you carry it to money in collaboration with the venture’s leads.
Own product positioning and the customer-facing materials that support it
— product sheets, decks, demo strategies — across multiple ventures simultaneously.
Turn what customers tell you into product direction.
You are the person who helps the venture clarify the reasons to adjust their strategy in response to market needs, and collect the evidence that justifies it.
Run customer discovery and find the next market
— new applications and adjacent segments for ventures that are starting to get traction.
Represent ventures externally
at industry events, partner meetings, and customer conversations.
Mentor and directly work alongside our venture leads
as the commercial half of each venture team.

What We're Looking For

Requirements

5+ years of experience
in business development, product management, or strategy within a startup environment.
You have taken a technical product to a paying customer.
A purchase order, a paid pilot, a signed design win, a contract. Tell us what it was, who bought it, and what they paid. Grants, non-dilutive funding, maturation envelopes, accelerator awards and research scholarships are all valuable, but direct customer engagement is critical.
PhD/M.Sc/M.Eng degree or equivalent research-level technical fluency.
You can hold a real conversation with hardware engineers, ML researchers, or physicists — and are able to provide guidance on their technology strategy.
Professional French and English.

You have worked in ambiguity
— as a product lead, founding PM, co-founder, applications or solutions engineer, or the first commercial hire at an early-stage company.

Also true of the people who thrive at TandemLaunch

Genuine curiosity about novel technology.
You are comfortable navigating low-information environments to develop a strategy.
You are honest about what you do not know.

You might be coming from

Technical product management at a hardware or ML company · the first commercial hire at a deep-tech startup · applications or solutions engineering · product marketing for a technical product · technical sales or business development in B2B hardware · a founding team where you owned go-to-market.

What We Offer

A seat at one of very few venture studios globally with 15+ years of track record in deep tech.
Cross-portfolio exposure — ventures spanning AI, sensors, hardware, materials and audio in your first year.
Participation in fund economics through TandemLaunch's employee incentive pool — long-term upside that grows with the portfolio.
Direct mentorship from operators — co-founders, product leads and CEOs across the portfolio.
A supportive team that values curiosity, initiative and collaboration.

The opportunity

Are you motivated by the chance to help ensure all young people in Canada can access mental health support and Feel Out Loud? Kids Help Phone (KHP) is Canada’s Unlock The Hope Youth Charity. We’re the first and Canada's only national 24/7, free, confidential, and multilingual e-mental health service for youth and a global leader in innovation for youth and their well-being.

The Senior Director, Data Governance and Management leads Kids Help Phone’s enterprise data strategy, governance, and management functions, ensuring data is governed, protected, and leveraged as a strategic asset. Reporting to the EVP, Technology & Data, this role is accountable for data governance, quality, stewardship, architecture, analytics governance, lifecycle management, responsible data use, and AI readiness.

Working across leadership, clinical services, research, privacy, legal, and operational teams, the Senior Director establishes enterprise standards, drives the evolution of KHP’s Data Operating Model, and strengthens organizational data capabilities. The role provides strategic leadership on data-related risks, opportunities, and investments, ensuring data practices support organizational goals, innovation, service excellence, and the trust of youth seeking support. It’ll take courage, collaboration, innovation, resilience and trust. If you’re interested in transforming e-mental health solutions with KHP, you can explore this opportunity today!

The responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy:

Develop and lead KHP’s enterprise data strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligning data, analytics, and AI capabilities with organizational priorities.

Define the vision for data governance, architecture, quality, accessibility, and responsible AI adoption.

Advise senior leadership on emerging trends, opportunities, risks, and investments related to data and AI.

Enterprise Leadership & Decision Authority:

Serve as the organization’s senior leader for data governance and management.

Establish enterprise data standards, accountability frameworks, and governance requirements.

Provide strategic guidance on data-related risks, investments, priorities, and key organizational decisions.

Resolve complex, cross-functional issues related to data ownership, quality, metrics, and reporting.

Data Governance & Operating Model:

Lead and evolve KHP’s Data Operating Model, governance frameworks, and enterprise-wide adoption.

Establish clear roles, responsibilities, and decision-making processes for data governance and stewardship.

Identify and mitigate emerging data, technology, and AI-related risks.

Drive KHP’s data transformation journey, advancing organizational data maturity and governance capabilities.

Data Ownership & Stewardship:

Lead the enterprise data stewardship program across business and service areas.

Define stewardship practices, training, and accountability expectations.

Resolve cross-functional issues related to data ownership, quality, access, lifecycle management, and reporting.

Data Quality, Metrics & Analytics:

Oversee data quality, reporting, business intelligence, and analytics governance.

Establish standards for critical data elements, business definitions, metrics, and reporting consistency.

Advance data and analytics capabilities to support evidence-based decision-making and innovation.

Oversee internal staff and external vendor support for ongoing development, optimization, and maintenance of data infrastructure and pipelines

Data Sources, Lifecycle & Responsible Use:

Define governance requirements for data sourcing, retention, lifecycle management, and responsible use.

Support governance processes for research, data sharing, analytics, AI-enabled initiatives, and regulatory compliance.

Ensure data practices align with privacy, security, legal, and ethical standards.

Governance, Adoption & Organizational Capability:

Chair enterprise data governance and stewardship forums and drive accountability across the organization.

Monitor adoption of governance practices and report on key risks, outcomes, and performance measures.

Lead stakeholder engagement, communications, and training to strengthen enterprise data literacy and capability.

Provide leadership and oversight for data governance programs, priorities, resources, and investments.

The qualifications

Minimum 12 years of progressively senior experience in data governance, data management, analytics, information management or related enterprise data disciplines, including significant experience in senior leadership roles with enterprise-wide accountability. 

Demonstrated leadership experience overseeing complex data, governance or operating-model transformation programs and leading program or project delivery professionals. 

Demonstrated experience designing or operationalizing a data governance framework, stewardship model, decision-rights model or enterprise data standards. 

Strong understanding of data ownership, stewardship, data definitions, data quality, metadata, lineage, lifecycle and metric governance. 

Experience optimizing and modernizing data architecture to enhance reliability, consistency and availability of data to end users. 

Demonstrated experience leading leaders and multidisciplinary teams, including establishing functional strategy, organizational capabilities, performance expectations and succession plans. 

Experience facilitating cross-functional decisions where business, technology, privacy, legal, risk and operational perspectives must be reconciled. 

Experience advising executives and senior governance bodies on complex data strategy, risk, investment and organizational decisions. 

Experience overseeing significant vendor relationships, technology investments and/or enterprise transformation budgets. 

Strong understanding of modern data platforms, cloud data architecture, analytics and BI ecosystems, including platforms such as Power BI and Databricks, and the governance implications of emerging AI capabilities. 

Ability to convert complex governance, risk and technical requirements into practical roles, standards, workflows and decision tools. 

Strong written communication, facilitation, stakeholder management and executive presentation skills. 

Sound judgement when working with sensitive information, ambiguity and competing organizational priorities. 

University degree in data/information management, computer science, information systems, business, engineering, health informatics or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of advanced professional experience and education. Graduate-level education is an asset. 

Preferred / Advantageous

Demonstrated experience operating in complex, highly sensitive or regulated data environments; experience with health, clinical, youth or similarly sensitive data environments strongly preferred.

The opportunity

Are you motivated by the chance to help ensure all young people in Canada can access mental health support and Feel Out Loud? Kids Help Phone (KHP) is Canada’s Unlock The Hope Youth Charity. We’re the first and Canada's only national 24/7, free, confidential, and multilingual e-mental health service for youth and a global leader in innovation for youth and their well-being.

The Senior Director, Data Governance and Management leads Kids Help Phone’s enterprise data strategy, governance, and management functions, ensuring data is governed, protected, and leveraged as a strategic asset. Reporting to the EVP, Technology & Data, this role is accountable for data governance, quality, stewardship, architecture, analytics governance, lifecycle management, responsible data use, and AI readiness.

Working across leadership, clinical services, research, privacy, legal, and operational teams, the Senior Director establishes enterprise standards, drives the evolution of KHP’s Data Operating Model, and strengthens organizational data capabilities. The role provides strategic leadership on data-related risks, opportunities, and investments, ensuring data practices support organizational goals, innovation, service excellence, and the trust of youth seeking support. It’ll take courage, collaboration, innovation, resilience and trust. If you’re interested in transforming e-mental health solutions with KHP, you can explore this opportunity today!

The responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy:

Develop and lead KHP’s enterprise data strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligning data, analytics, and AI capabilities with organizational priorities.

Define the vision for data governance, architecture, quality, accessibility, and responsible AI adoption.

Advise senior leadership on emerging trends, opportunities, risks, and investments related to data and AI.

Enterprise Leadership & Decision Authority:

Serve as the organization’s senior leader for data governance and management.

Establish enterprise data standards, accountability frameworks, and governance requirements.

Provide strategic guidance on data-related risks, investments, priorities, and key organizational decisions.

Resolve complex, cross-functional issues related to data ownership, quality, metrics, and reporting.

Data Governance & Operating Model:

Lead and evolve KHP’s Data Operating Model, governance frameworks, and enterprise-wide adoption.

Establish clear roles, responsibilities, and decision-making processes for data governance and stewardship.

Identify and mitigate emerging data, technology, and AI-related risks.

Drive KHP’s data transformation journey, advancing organizational data maturity and governance capabilities.

Data Ownership & Stewardship:

Lead the enterprise data stewardship program across business and service areas.

Define stewardship practices, training, and accountability expectations.

Resolve cross-functional issues related to data ownership, quality, access, lifecycle management, and reporting.

Data Quality, Metrics & Analytics:

Oversee data quality, reporting, business intelligence, and analytics governance.

Establish standards for critical data elements, business definitions, metrics, and reporting consistency.

Advance data and analytics capabilities to support evidence-based decision-making and innovation.

Oversee internal staff and external vendor support for ongoing development, optimization, and maintenance of data infrastructure and pipelines

Data Sources, Lifecycle & Responsible Use:

Define governance requirements for data sourcing, retention, lifecycle management, and responsible use.

Support governance processes for research, data sharing, analytics, AI-enabled initiatives, and regulatory compliance.

Ensure data practices align with privacy, security, legal, and ethical standards.

Governance, Adoption & Organizational Capability:

Chair enterprise data governance and stewardship forums and drive accountability across the organization.

Monitor adoption of governance practices and report on key risks, outcomes, and performance measures.

Lead stakeholder engagement, communications, and training to strengthen enterprise data literacy and capability.

Provide leadership and oversight for data governance programs, priorities, resources, and investments.

The qualifications

Minimum 12 years of progressively senior experience in data governance, data management, analytics, information management or related enterprise data disciplines, including significant experience in senior leadership roles with enterprise-wide accountability. 

Demonstrated leadership experience overseeing complex data, governance or operating-model transformation programs and leading program or project delivery professionals. 

Demonstrated experience designing or operationalizing a data governance framework, stewardship model, decision-rights model or enterprise data standards. 

Strong understanding of data ownership, stewardship, data definitions, data quality, metadata, lineage, lifecycle and metric governance. 

Experience optimizing and modernizing data architecture to enhance reliability, consistency and availability of data to end users. 

Demonstrated experience leading leaders and multidisciplinary teams, including establishing functional strategy, organizational capabilities, performance expectations and succession plans. 

Experience facilitating cross-functional decisions where business, technology, privacy, legal, risk and operational perspectives must be reconciled. 

Experience advising executives and senior governance bodies on complex data strategy, risk, investment and organizational decisions. 

Experience overseeing significant vendor relationships, technology investments and/or enterprise transformation budgets. 

Strong understanding of modern data platforms, cloud data architecture, analytics and BI ecosystems, including platforms such as Power BI and Databricks, and the governance implications of emerging AI capabilities. 

Ability to convert complex governance, risk and technical requirements into practical roles, standards, workflows and decision tools. 

Strong written communication, facilitation, stakeholder management and executive presentation skills. 

Sound judgement when working with sensitive information, ambiguity and competing organizational priorities. 

University degree in data/information management, computer science, information systems, business, engineering, health informatics or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of advanced professional experience and education. Graduate-level education is an asset. 

Preferred / Advantageous

Demonstrated experience operating in complex, highly sensitive or regulated data environments; experience with health, clinical, youth or similarly sensitive data environments strongly preferred. 

Knowledge of Canadian privacy requirements, research governance, Indigenous data governance and responsible AI governance. 

Experience governing enterprise metrics, reporting products, Power BI, cloud data platforms, data catalogues or lineage capabilities. 

Relevant certification or training such as DAMA/CDMP, DCAM, privacy, risk, audit or data management certification. 

Experience establishing a new governance function and transitioning responsibilities from a transformation program into ongoing operations. 

Don’t meet every qualification listed? Studies often report equity-deserving people are less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every requirement. KHP is dedicated to building a more diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role, but your experience doesn’t align with every qualification, we welcome you to apply anyway. You may have the qualifications / experience for this role or other opportunities at KHP!

The application process

To apply for this opportunity, you can tap the “Apply” button on this page and follow the on-screen instructions.

About KHP, Canada’s Unlock The Hope Youth Charity

Kids Help Phone (KHP) is Canada’s only free, national, 24/7, multilingual and confidential e-mental health service for youth to get help and Feel Out Loud. Since 1989, KHP has been the empowering, trusted changemaker giving young people’s feelings, big and small, a non-judgmental place to go through personalized well-being solutions. A made-in-Canada, global leader, KHP continually evolves by blending data, innovation and technology with real human support and clinical knowledge to unlock the hope young people need to thrive in their world. Inclusion, Diversity, Equity and Accessibility (IDEA)

KHP has a long history of celebrating and advancing IDEA through our tailored programs, services, policies, initiatives and task forces with contributions and leadership from teams across the organization. We believe it’s critical that our services empower everyone who interacts with us to bring their authentic selves to an environment of mutual respect. An open and diverse community can foster the inclusion and amplification of voices that have been, and continue to be, underrepresented. 

As such, we welcome applicants from equity-deserving communities (e.g. Indigenous Peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ+ individuals, etc.). We strongly believe that alleviating the underrepresentation of equity-deserving groups will help create a stronger KHP and help us better support the needs of youth from coast to coast to coast.

Create one integrated Product + Tech operating model

Build a high-performing, AI-native Product + Tech organization

Establish a clear and commercially focused product and technology strategy
.
Create stronger alignment between Product, Engineering, Commercial, Operations, and other functions.
Improve speed, quality, and predictability of product delivery
while maintaining appropriate technology and security standards.
Increase adoption and measurable business impact from product investments.

Establish AI and data as meaningful business capabilities rather than standalone initiatives.
Build a strong, accountable leadership team with clear ownership across Product and Technology.
